Key Takeaways

D-Wave Quantum shares fell 18% today alongside Rigetti Computing and IonQ, with no D-Wave news behind the drop.

Quantum stocks are trading as high-beta bets on tech risk, and Wednesday's chip selloff carried into Thursday.

D-Wave needs $36.5 million of second-half revenue to hit analysts' $42.5 million for 2026.

IBM launched a quantum error-correction platform with Oak Ridge National Laboratory today, a reminder of how deep-pocketed D-Wave's rivals are.

D-Wave Quantum (QBTS:NASDAQ) fell 18% this morning, and it had company: Rigetti Computing (RGTI:NASDAQ) is down 18%, and IonQ (IONQ:NYSE) is down 15%.

The morning's one real quantum headline came from a far bigger company. IBM (IBM:NYSE) said it and AMD launched a quantum error-correction platform with Oak Ridge National Laboratory, tied to the Department of Energy's Quantum Genesis Mission.

Quantum trades as one big bet

D-Wave put out no news. The pressure came from chip stocks: Intel, Nvidia and AMD extended a selloff that began Wednesday, after Democrats' larger-than-expected midterm wins.

Quantum stocks burn cash, and investors are paying today for revenue that's years away, so they trade as high-beta bets on tech's mood. In October, D-Wave even fell when IonQ priced a $2 billion stock sale.

TIKR tracks 17 analysts on D-Wave Quantum. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on D-Wave Quantum, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See D-Wave Quantum's Analyst Ratings

The revenue still has to show up

Analysts expect D-Wave's revenue to climb steeply from a small base:

D-Wave Quantum (QBTS): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, fiscal 2022-2028 (TIKR)

That puts a lot of weight on the fourth quarter. D-Wave brought in $5.9 million in the first half of 2026, so the second half needs $36.5 million. Management expects both of this year's system shipments to go out in the fourth quarter, including Florida Atlantic University's $20 million machine. And revenue has come in below consensus three quarters running.

Nothing today should move those estimates. D-Wave's next report could.

Before today's drop, D-Wave traded at 58x forward sales, well under its three-year average of 152x:

D-Wave Quantum (QBTS): forward (NTM) price/sales, last 3 years (TIKR)

That's still a steep price for $3.08 million of second-quarter revenue. D-Wave had $546.2 million of cash and securities at June 30, so it isn't under pressure today, though it burned $79.0 million of free cash flow in the first half.

IBM has much deeper pockets

IBM's news is a longer-term problem for D-Wave. IBM generated $7.8 billion of free cash flow in the first nine months of 2026, and now it's working with a national lab on error correction. D-Wave is going after the same problem with its gate-model program, which targets 2032. D-Wave won Commerce Department funding in September. Can it win Department of Energy work too?

title: Can D-Wave Quantum Stock Fall 50%?

Can D-Wave Quantum Stock Fall 50%?

D-Wave Quantum (QBTS) stock fell 34.3% in the month ending November 4, 2026. Shares of IonQ and Rigetti Computing also dropped during that period, while the S&P 500 slipped 1.6%. IonQ lost 31.8% and Rigetti 26.1% over the same dates. The decline left D-Wave at $10.38, which is 67.8% below its highest close of the past year. A 50% fall would not be new for D-Wave. From the November 4 close of $10.38, a drop of that size would leave the shares near $5.19. The stock lost 50% or more from its high to its low in three of the five market shocks it has traded through. How did those falls compare with the market's, and how long did D-Wave take to recover?

D-Wave Has Fallen Far Deeper Than The S&P 500

D-Wave suffered its worst fall in a market shock during the Summer-Fall 2023 Five Percent Yield Shock. The stock lost 73.0% at that time, compared with a 9.5% drop for the S&P 500. Across all five shocks, D-Wave fell an average of 51.2%, against 11.3% for the index over the same dates.

The stock climbed back to its pre-fall high after all five shocks, with a median recovery time of 3.0 months from the low. Two recoveries took more than a year, however. The climb back from the 2023 yield shock took 12.9 months, and the rebound from the 2022 inflation and Fed tightening shock took 30.7 months. D-Wave only began trading on August 8, 2022, partway through that earlier shock.

Does D-Wave Have Enough Cash To Fund Losses?

The company has enough cash for now, though its operating losses are far larger than a year ago. D-Wave held $546 million in cash and short-term investments against $48.1 million of debt at the end of June 2026. That cash was down from $819.3 million a year earlier, mostly because D-Wave paid about $250 million in cash for Quantum Circuits in January 2026, management said.

D-Wave is also burning cash faster. The company used $120 million of free cash flow over the twelve months ending in June 2026, more than double the $53.3 million from a year earlier. Combined with the roughly $250 million deal, that spending outpaces the $273.1 million drop in cash, indicating some money also came in from other sources.

Revenue has not grown alongside the spending. D-Wave reported $3.08 million in revenue for the second quarter of 2026, essentially flat on a year earlier. The operating loss for the quarter reached $53.3 million, about twice the $26.5 million reported a year before. Measured against sales, the twelve-month operating loss through June 2026 was D-Wave's widest at any quarter-end since the end of 2021.
